question: In Python, an if statement requires a colon (:) at the end of its condition.
Python's if statement can have more than one else clause.
Using multiple 'elif' clauses in an if-else chain is equivalent to using multiple independent if statements.
Indentation is not necessary in Python if statements when semicolons are used to separate statements.
The condition in an if statement can be any expression that evaluates to a Boolean value or a truthy/falsy value.
Python allows you to write an if statement and its associated single statement on the same line.
An if statement without an else clause in Python will result in a syntax error.
Using a non-Boolean value as the condition in a Python if statement will always result in a TypeError.
The following code snippet will raise a syntax error: if (x > 10) print('x is large')
A chained if-elif-else block in Python evaluates conditions sequentially and stops after executing the block for the first true condition.
